function_v0.doc:
Add PT coupon capacity: pull `amount` USDC, wrap to SR, strip into PT+YT held by the vault.
Pure capacity \xe2\x80\x94 it creates **no liability**.

**Admin-gated.** v1's `seed` was permissionless, which is what turned a capacity limit into
`tofix.md` #18's denial-of-service: anyone could prepend dust positions until the redeem
walk exceeded the transaction budget and every receipt became unpayable. There is no walk
here, but an open `seed` still lets a stranger write vault state for the price of a
transaction, and nothing needs it to be open.
function_v0.name: seed

function_v0.doc: What `amount` USDC would earn: `(payout, coupon, rate_bps)`. Read-only.
function_v0.name: quote

function_v0.doc:
Recover surplus inventory \xe2\x80\x94 seed capital and unneeded capacity \xe2\x80\x94 to `to`.

**Liability-gated**, which is `tofix.md` #22: v1 had no path at all, so seed capital and any
over-provisioned inventory were one-way. This releases only PT face **above** every open
payout, so it can never touch a receipt's backing. Admin only.
function_v0.name: sweep

function_v0.doc:
Redeem a matured receipt for its full promised payout.

**O(1) \xe2\x80\x94 and that is the headline difference from v1.** v1 walked a list of wrapper
positions, redeeming each until the payout was met, at ~7 MB per position; five positions
exhausted the mainnet transaction budget and a stranger could inflate the list at will
(`tofix.md` #18). Here PT is fungible bearer, so the vault burns `payout` PT face in one
`redeem_py` call. Cost does not depend on history, on how the inventory was assembled, or
on anything an attacker controls.
function_v0.name: redeem

function_v0.doc:
Lock a fixed rate. Pulls `amount` USDC, mints matching PT+YT into inventory, and issues a
receipt promising `principal + coupon` at maturity.

The coupon is backed out of **existing** capacity: the deposit itself only creates PT equal
to the principal, so the coupon must come from spare inventory. That is why the capacity
check is the load-bearing line \xe2\x80\x94 it is what makes the promise solvent rather than hopeful.
function_v0.name: deposit

function_v0.doc:
Claim the vault's YT yield and reinvest it as fresh PT capacity.

**No maturity gate and no pruning**, which is `tofix.md` #21. v1's `harvest` refused to run
after maturity and pruned positions that still held live YT, so yield accrued before
maturity became permanently unclaimable. Here the engine keeps pre-expiry yield claimable
forever, and this simply collects it whenever it is called.

Returns `(sr_claimed, py_minted)`. Reinvestment is skipped past expiry (the engine refuses
`mint_py` then, correctly) \xe2\x80\x94 the claimed SR stays as vault inventory instead of reverting
and throwing the claim away with it.
function_v0.name: harvest

function_v0.doc: What [`Self::sweep_surplus`] would release right now, without moving anything.
function_v0.name: surplus

function_v0.doc:
One-shot, admin-gated init.

Takes **only** the engine address. sr, pt, underlying and maturity are read back from it, so
the `tofix.md` #24 class of mismatch \xe2\x80\x94 a vault wired to an asset its PT does not redeem into
\xe2\x80\x94 cannot be constructed here.

Recover surplus **SR, YT and USDC** to `to`, at or after expiry (`tofix.md` #22).

`sweep` handles the PT leg. This handles everything else the vault ends up holding, which
the PT-only sweep left permanently stranded \xe2\x80\x94 measured at **248.53 SR** on a 20,000 USDC
seed, about 1.2% of it, plus the USDC flooring remainder.

PT face is directly comparable to a payout, so surplus PT can be identified \xe2\x80\x94 and released \xe2\x80\x94
at any time. The other three legs cannot:

forward value that `assert_solvent` cannot see, because that invariant compares PT face
against liability and says nothing about future capacity. A pre-expiry YT sweep would
quietly degrade the vault's ability to meet later payouts while every check still passed.

udt_struct_v0.name: Receipt

fields.doc:
USDC already collected toward `payout` by earlier partial redemptions (`tofix.md` #20).

A redeem sizes its PT burn to what the venue can actually pay, banks the proceeds here, and
pays the holder only once `collected >= payout`. Until then this USDC sits in the vault
**reserved for this receipt** \xe2\x80\x94 it is counted by `assert_solvent` in place of the PT that was
burned to obtain it, and excluded from every sweep.
fields.name: collected

fields.doc: USDC guaranteed at maturity = principal + fixed coupon. Backed 1:1 by PT face.
fields.name: payout

fields.doc: USDC the user deposited.
fields.name: principal

fields.doc: The APR quoted, in bps. Display only \xe2\x80\x94 `payout` is the binding number.
fields.name: rate_bps

fields.doc:
PT face burned by this receipt's partial redemptions that did **not** turn into banked USDC
(`anyfix.md` F2).

Each partial leg burns `take` PT and banks `got <= take` USDC, because both conversions on
the way out (`PT -> SR -> USDC`) floor. The gap is a genuine loss of vault inventory, about
a stroop a leg. Recording it is what lets [`SrVault::assert_solvent`] tell expected rounding
residue apart from a real deficit \xe2\x80\x94 before this, the third partial leg on any receipt
tripped the invariant and the receipt could not be redeemed at all until the venue could pay
the whole remainder in one call.

Released from the running total when the receipt closes, so the slack never outlives the
receipt that earned it.
fields.name: residue

udt_struct_v0.doc:
A single deposit's accounting record \xe2\x80\x94 the unit that makes Spield's yield math correct.

**Per-position, never overwritten** (fixes SCF #4): every `mint` creates a *new* `Position`
with its own `entry_rate`, so topping up never clobbers an earlier tranche's entry point.

**`settled_rate` travels with the YT** (fixes SCF #5/#6): yield is always measured from
`settled_rate`, which starts at `entry_rate` and is bumped to the current rate on every
`claim_yield` *without burning YT*. A position transferred to a new owner carries its
`settled_rate`, so the buyer can only ever claim yield accrued *after* they held it.
udt_struct_v0.name: Position

fields.doc: Blend `b_rate` (SCALAR_12) at the moment this position was minted. Immutable.
fields.name: entry_rate

fields.doc: False once the position is fully redeemed/closed (all PT + YT gone).
fields.name: open

fields.doc: Current owner of this position (and of the PT + YT it represents).
fields.name: owner

fields.doc: Underlying principal deposited for this position, in the underlying's decimals (USDC).\nEqual to the PT amount still outstanding and the YT amount still outstanding (1:1:1 at\nmint; PT and YT are only reduced by `redeem_pt` / `combine_and_redeem`).
fields.name: principal

fields.doc: PT still held in this position. Burned on `redeem_pt` (after maturity) and on `combine`.
fields.name: pt_amount

fields.doc: Blend `b_rate` (SCALAR_12) up to which yield has already been settled/paid. Starts equal\nto `entry_rate`; advanced to `current_rate` on each claim. Yield owed is measured from\nhere, so the same YT can be claimed across many epochs.
fields.name: settled_rate

fields.doc: Blend bToken shares this position is backed by (its slice of the wrapper's total Blend\nposition). `principal = shares * entry_rate / SCALAR_12` at mint.
fields.name: shares

fields.doc: YT still held in this position. **Never burned by `claim_yield`** \xe2\x80\x94 only by `combine`.
fields.name: yt_amount

udt_struct_v0.doc:
Defence-in-depth bound on `b_rate` reads, stored in the strategy adapter's config.

The bound is **time-aware**: `b_rate` may rise by at most `max_apr_bps` per year, pro-rated by
the seconds elapsed since `last_ts`. This makes the check independent of how often the strategy
is read (a long-untouched position no longer false-trips), so only `max_apr_bps` \xe2\x80\x94 calibrated
against Blend's real max borrow APR \xe2\x80\x94 needs tuning. See [`crate::math::check_rate_bound_timed`].
udt_struct_v0.name: RateBound

fields.doc: Last `b_rate` the strategy observed (SCALAR_12). Used to enforce monotonicity + the ceiling.
fields.name: last_rate

fields.doc: Unix-second timestamp at which `last_rate` was observed. The elapsed time since this is what\nthe allowed increase is pro-rated by. `0` = no observation yet (first read bypasses the cap).
fields.name: last_ts

fields.doc: Max allowed **annual** `b_rate` growth, in basis points (e.g. `30_000` = 300% APR). Set\ngenerously above Blend's real max borrow APR so honest reads always pass.
fields.name: max_apr_bps

udt_struct_v0.doc:
A single Fixed-Rate Vault deposit (plan \xc2\xa711.2 / \xc2\xa77.5 \xe2\x80\x94 the flagship "lock X% fixed" product).

PT-passthrough model: the user deposits `principal` USDC and is promised exactly `payout`
USDC at maturity (`payout = principal + coupon`, the coupon being the fixed return). The
vault backs every receipt with **PT it actually holds** (each PT redeems 1:1 at maturity),
so the fixed rate is solvent by construction \xe2\x80\x94 the same rigor as the wrapper's invariant.
There is no per-user yield accounting here: the user's outcome is fixed and known at deposit.
udt_struct_v0.name: FixedReceipt

fields.doc: False once redeemed.

fields.doc: Owner of this receipt (the only account that may redeem it).
fields.name: owner

fields.doc: USDC the user is guaranteed at maturity = principal + fixed coupon. Backed by PT the\nvault holds 1:1, so it is always redeemable.
fields.name: payout

fields.doc: USDC principal the user deposited.
fields.name: principal

fields.doc: The fixed APR quoted for this receipt, in basis points (for display / events only \xe2\x80\x94 the\neconomically binding figure is `payout`).
fields.name: rate_bps
